model: The person I'd like to talk about is Jane Goodall, the scientist who spent decades studying chimpanzees in Tanzania. She's definitely someone I look up to, even though I've never met her and probably never will. I first came across her in a documentary which my biology teacher showed us at school, and I've followed her work ever since. She's in her nineties now, but she's still travelling around the world, giving talks and encouraging young people to protect the environment. Obviously she has a huge following, but what strikes me most is how down-to-earth she seems. In interviews she never talks down to people, and she really goes out of her way to answer children's questions properly. I think that's what makes her a real role model rather than just a famous name. She's also someone who changed her whole field. Back then, scientists who studied animals were expected to use numbers instead of names, but she gave every chimp a name and treated them as individuals, which was quite controversial at the time. These days I'm trying to live a bit more sustainably, and I suppose some of her attitude has rubbed off on me. I'm cutting down on plastic, and I'm reading more about conservation. So even though we're complete strangers, she's influenced the way I think quite a lot.
